::: {.digest-item}
**[RFC 9889: A Realization of Network Slices for 5G Networks Using Current IP/MPLS Technologies](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9889/)**

<span class="digest-source">IETF · RFC</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> The first RFC that specifies how to realize 5G network slices on existing IP/MPLS transport. It maps the 3GPP slice construct onto the fabric operators already run — service chaining, EVPN, segment routing — and lays out how a slice request flows from the core down to the transport plane. It is the reference for what "a slice" concretely means when it hits the network, rather than staying a core-side abstraction.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> A rare IETF/3GPP convergence artifact. Directly relevant to slice management and Private 5G over existing fabrics — worth reading before designing any slice-management plane.

<span class="digest-tags">#private-5g · #slicing · #ip-mpls</span>
:::

::: {.digest-item}
**[A Network Digital Twin of a 5G Private Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.12458)**

<span class="digest-source">arXiv</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> A full digital twin of a 5G private network — RAN plus core — covering data collection, device control, and the mapping of physical elements to their digital counterparts. Notable because it treats the *whole* network (not just the RAN) as the twin, and walks through the synchronization and control loops that keep the twin faithful.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> Exactly at the intersection: Private 5G + digital twins + network intelligence. A concrete reference architecture to critique.

<span class="digest-tags">#digital-twin · #private-5g</span>
:::

::: {.digest-item}
**[AI-Native Network Digital Twin for Intelligent Network Management](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01584)**

<span class="digest-source">arXiv</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> Proposes an AI-native network digital twin for intelligent network management in the 5G → 6G transition. The key claim: the twin is not just a simulation sandbox, but the substrate on which the management and optimization AI runs — perception, prediction, and closed-loop control all operate through the twin.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> The "intelligent network management" axis of your thesis, condensed into one paper.

<span class="digest-tags">#digital-twin · #network-management · #6g</span>
:::

::: {.digest-item}
**[Ollama](https://ollama.com/)**

<span class="digest-source">Ollama</span>

<span class="lbl tldr">TLDR</span> The de-facto local LLM runtime: pull and serve models with one command, with a simple OpenAI-compatible API on top. It wraps llama.cpp, so it inherits the GGML quantization story that makes 7B+ models runnable on a laptop or an edge box.

<span class="lbl why">Why read it</span> The fastest way to stand up a local inference stack for edge experiments.

<span class="digest-tags">#edge-inference · #local-llm</span>
:::
